rationale: A wins because it mostly keeps its hands on the supplied facts and turns them into usable newsroom lanes. Its strongest line, "Duolingo puts its new AI feature behind a paywall and its new course out front for free," is a clean business-model story. B has sharper teeth in places, but "people are talking to its cartoon owl" is a basic product error: Lily is not the owl, and a founder cannot afford that kind of cute wrongness in a pitch.
gaps_in_A: "Duolingo says engagement is at an all-time high" overstates the supplied fact. The update says DAU hit a new high, not engagement overall.
"a live public educator critique of gamification" implies a current critique. The update only says some educators have publicly criticized gamification, with no date or live peg.
"Record DAU, profitable, two new product bets in the same quarter" adds quarter framing not supplied in the update.
The paywall angle and markets angle overlap more than A admits; both lean on the free chess/paid AI split plus public-company monetization logic.
gaps_in_B: "people are talking to its cartoon owl" is wrong. The supplied character is Lily, not Duolingo's owl.
"9 minutes per session in beta is a long time" declares significance before providing the baseline B correctly says it needs.
"live, unscripted spoken conversation" adds "unscripted," which is not in the update.
"the set has no current news signal anchoring it" is strategically backwards. The update itself is a same-day launch with DAU and beta-engagement numbers.
